home.intro: I'm Paynalton, though almost everyone calls me Pay. I develop software, design solutions and support teams to solve problems. I'm interested in projects that require learning and connecting disciplines. I work with people and AI agents to expand what we can understand and build, from enterprise systems to tools for editorial creation.
home.projectsIntro: Every project starts with a specific need. These cases show how I approach system integration, the modernization of an operation and the development of tools to think and create with artificial intelligence.
home.onixSummary: I developed an ERP for a corporation that needed to overcome problems with data integrity and networked work. Years later I returned to modernize the code and infrastructure, maintaining the continuity of a tool that continues to support its operations.
home.guacamayaSummary: I developed GUACAMAYA to support the creation and publication of a book. It combines local and remote tools and agents under author control. It continues to develop while I use it to explore, write and prepare new works.

page.projectsIntro: These projects show different ways of solving problems: integrating services, replacing legacy systems, responding to unexpected changes, and creating tools to work with AI. In each case I explain my involvement, the main decisions, and the status of the solution.
page.experienceIntro: My career does not follow a single specialty. I have moved from support and automation to systems development, architecture, and team leadership. In each stage I have sought to understand operations and take on the necessary responsibilities to ensure the solution works, from code to its maintenance.
page.worksIntro: I write to explore ideas and experiences that do not always find their place in a technical explanation. Here I gather essays, fiction, and editorial projects in progress. Some pieces were born years ago, and others are growing alongside my work with AI. Each piece retains its voice, its context, and its status: a finished publication, an available chapter, or a story that I'm still building.
page.aboutIntro: I am Pay: developer, reader, and author in continuous training. I enjoy understanding problems, connecting ideas, and building solutions. Between software and writing, I explore how we think, what makes us human, and what we can create together with other people and artificial intelligence.
home.skillsIntro: I organize my experience by the problems I can address: building applications, connecting systems, preparing for their operation, and helping other people work on them. Technologies are tools I choose according to the context; my practice requires learning and adapting when needs change.
home.methodIntro: I enjoy problems because they force me to understand something I still don't know. My process combines research, decisions tailored to available resources, and verification of the result. With people or agents, I seek to maintain clarity about what we are trying to solve.
home.experienceIntro:
I'm Paynalton and I sign my work with that name. My background includes fullstack development, solution architecture, system integration, and team leadership. I adapt to the needs of the project and participate in both technical decisions and implementation and operations.

I started programming at twelve with MS Basic. Before taking my first formal developer position in 2009, I was already building personal projects and tools to automate tasks in other jobs. That habit of learning by solving problems continues to guide my work.

I've created enterprise systems, campaign platforms, and services that evolved from urgent needs. I've also led development teams, with responsibilities for hiring, training, architecture, and delivery. Currently, I'm exploring how to work with AI agents while preserving human judgment and building tools that allow for maintaining the context of complex tasks.
page.contactIntro: I'm interested in projects that require understanding a problem, connecting different disciplines, and building a solution. If you're looking to collaborate in development, architecture, working with agents, or editorial creation, you can write to me. Tell me what you're trying to solve, where you are in the process, and what you hope to achieve; that context helps start the conversation.
page.termsIntro: A topic can appear in a project, a professional experience, or a work. Explore those connections to know different ways of approaching it. Each relationship indicates whether a content applies a technology, demonstrates a capability, or develops a reflection.
page.bookSummary: An exploration of the relationship between human thought and artificial intelligence. The book proposes working with AI as an additional cognitive component to expand our capabilities, while preserving judgment and direction of what we want to understand and create.

about.bio:
I go by Pay and sign my work as Paynalton. My curiosity usually starts with a question: Why does it work this way? When a problem appears, I want to understand it, break it down, and find a way to solve it. The subject may change; the impulse is quite constant. Perhaps that's why I enjoy developing software so much: there's always another problem waiting.

I started programming at twelve years old and have been self-taught. Technology is an important part of my life, but my questions also extend into philosophy, literature, history, and nature. I'm interested in what it means to be human, how we recognize intelligence, and how our tools shape what we can think and do.

I write to explore those questions from different perspectives. Some take the form of essays; others need characters, conflicts, and imagined worlds. Working with artificial intelligence has expanded that exploration and led me to create tools to support it. I'm interested in preserving the human direction while learning to think with new interlocutors.

I see philosophy as an ongoing process. In my journey, the study of nihilism can lead to pessimism, and the need to move beyond it can bring me closer to stoicism. I don't see it as an obligatory path for everyone, but rather as a personal way of navigating ideas, examining them, and continuing forward.

I also find curiosity in everyday activities: repairing or building things, listening to music, reading, and playing video games. Humor accompanies me when I speak about serious problems. I like to learn without having to pretend I already know everything and to converse with people who allow me to see things from a perspective I hadn't considered.
about.interestsBody: Reading has changed the way I understand work, rules, friendship, and our place in nature. Some works gave me answers; others made me formulate questions that I continue to develop. I keep part of that journey on Goodreads.
about.musicBody: Music is also part of my everyday space. I share a selection for anyone who wants to know another part of my interests, beyond code and texts.
about.methodIntro: I enjoy problems because they force me to understand something I still don't know. My process combines research, decisions tailored to available resources, and verification of the result. With people or agents, I seek to maintain clarity about what we are trying to solve.
about.method1Body: I start by researching and understanding the technologies involved. I need to understand the problem deeply enough to distinguish a cause from its symptoms and to evaluate the consequences of a solution.
about.method2Body: I look for experiences from other people and review the solutions they applied. From there, I evaluate what can be reused and when it's necessary to design another response, considering the available resources and time.
about.method3Title: Learning as part of the work
about.method3Body: A new solution may require knowledge I do not yet have. Studying documentation and practicing are part of implementation. Learning matters when it helps me understand more clearly and make informed decisions.
about.method4Body: With a team, I pay attention to what is preventing progress. Listening to someone explain the problem can help them find the answer on their own. At other times, a pause and some distance allow for a clearer return.
about.method5Body: When I work with AI agents, I create intermediate documentation so they can reconstruct the context. This is especially important in long tasks, where decisions and their motivations must survive each interaction.
about.method6Body: After building the solution, I verify that the problem has been resolved. The delivery needs to be tested against the situation that motivated it and adjusted when tests or use show something different from what was expected.
about.reading1Body: This reading made me think about the resignation with which we can accept the deterioration of our environment. In the question "Who is John Galt?" I found an echo of our "that’s just how it is." The speech by Francisco d’Anconia on money led me to develop my own distinction between money and capital. I understand the latter as the effort that contributes to the survival of humanity, even if it doesn't produce income. Creating knowledge, tools, or capabilities can also have value from that perspective.
about.reading2Body: The idea of value tables helped me recognize that many rules, even those that are never written, have a history. My reading of rebellion changed: understanding a rule and subjecting it to judgment allows me to decide whether to keep it, discard it, or formulate another. This reflection interests me as part of the construction of judgment and of my own identity. It's not about ending thought, but about taking responsibility for continuing to examine it.
about.reading3Body: This book expanded my questions about behaviors we take for granted as inevitable. It led me to think about how recognizing a dynamic, taking distance, and seeking a conscious response can change our participation in it. It also transformed my understanding of friendship. In my reading, the desire for union with another person can take different paths: one of them involves intellectual affinity and a bond that evolves and matures. It's a personal reflection on intimacy and friendship that I continue to develop.
about.reading4Body: The difficulty of understanding an intelligence radically different from our own was what most impacted me. Reading it made me question what it means to be human, what characteristics define our species, and how I fit into it as an individual. It also made me think about humanity's place in nature and the connections that bind us to it. These are questions that continue to shape my interest in artificial intelligence and in other ways of understanding the world.
